Bedrock of marrow, sinew and fiber, tissue, tendon, joint, organ. Swimming slews of cell upon cell. Through this walking dance of living death gestures forth in trying times the protective instinct, calling out through pain, strain and danger's austere glance. You communicate in mind, to mind, the belief, buried deeply like perennial tendrils, that there is a definite me to preserve in and amongst the pullulating throng of this life's activity. Yet such a belief reaches out as but a thought, caught as it were between the body's limbs, and catching like a net the totality of perspectival thinking, carrying ashore the shoddy summation of ever flailing memory, vainly refortified over again against relentless decay. But one thought amongst the masses, you too are of the nature of coming and going, held hostage by the fear that I, in essence, actually am some thing that could be lost. But if I trace you back along your retreating sulk, back into the quietude of consciousness, where may I find it, this self-image you speak of so surely, so self sure, blasé and flippant? If I can watch you die, oh thought of great assumption, how can you be I? You are falsified in the very act of the mind's proclamation, so without a doubt I know that neither you are, nor are you not.
